title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree
summary: Given a weighted undirected connected graph with vertices numbered 0 to n-1, and an array of edges with their weights, identify the critical and pseudo-critical edges in the minimum spanning tree.
statement: Given a weighted undirected connected graph with vertices numbered 0 to n-1, and an array of edges with their weights, identify the critical and pseudo-critical edges in the minimum spanning tree. A critical edge, when removed, increases the MST weight. A pseudo-critical edge may appear in some MSTs but not all. Return the indices of these edges in any order.
constraints: The connected undirected graph has 2 through 100 vertices and at most 200 uniquely indexed edges.
An edge is critical if removing it raises the MST weight; it is pseudo-critical if some, but not every, MST contains it.
Return [critical_indices, pseudo_critical_indices], each in increasing input-index order.
hints: Compare every edge against the unconstrained MST weight.
Re-run Kruskal once excluding the edge and once forcing it first.
A higher exclusion cost means critical; otherwise equal forced cost means pseudo-critical.
These tests directly encode membership in all optimal trees versus at least one optimal tree.
editorial: These tests directly encode membership in all optimal trees versus at least one optimal tree.

tests.explanation: Edges zero and one occur in every minimum tree; edges two through five can each occur in at least one minimum tree.
Every edge belongs to some weight-three spanning tree, but none belongs to all of them.
